Pointwise RNX Agreement Across Neighborhood Sizes

Source: R/neighbor.R
pointwise_rnx.Rd

For each observation, compare which neighbors are shared by the reference and the embedding across neighborhood sizes.

Usage

pointwise_rnx(din, dout, k = NULL)

Arguments

din

Reference distance matrix.

dout

Distance matrix to compare with din.

k

Optional unique neighborhood sizes from 1 through n - 2, where n is the number of observations. Supply these sizes to return curve columns alongside the per-observation AUC. The default returns AUC only.

Value

A list with auc, a numeric vector in observation order, and curve, a matrix with one row per observation and columns rnx<k> in requested order, or NULL when k is omitted. Both retain the reference row names if present. The mean of auc equals rnx_auc(). The column means of curve equal rnx_curve() at the requested sizes, up to numerical precision.

Details

RNX adjusts nearest-neighbor overlap for chance. Its value at a single k is an affine transformation of overlap for that observation. The AUC averages RNX over every k from 1 through n - 2, weighting each value by 1 / k, regardless of the curve sizes requested.

Distances use the same exact ranking and column-order tie convention as rnx_curve(). Diagonal entries are excluded. A value of 1 means perfect agreement, 0 is the random-neighborhood baseline, and values can be negative.

Scaling

Supply two dense N by N distance matrices. At 5,000 observations their double entries use about 381.5 MiB together, before working storage. For Euclidean coordinates, exact_rank_profiles() ranks one query at a time. Set query_rows to score a sample against all other observations.

References

Lee et al. (2013) define the RNX curve. doi:10.1016/j.neucom.2012.12.036

Lee, Peluffo-Ordóñez and Verleysen (2015) summarize the curve across neighborhood sizes with weights proportional to 1 / k. doi:10.1016/j.neucom.2014.12.095

See also

pointwise_rank_preservation(), rnx_curve(), rnx_auc()

Examples

din <- as.matrix(dist(iris[, -5]))
dout <- as.matrix(dist(prcomp(iris[, -5], rank. = 2)$x))
scores <- pointwise_rnx(din, dout, k = c(5, 15, 40))
head(scores$auc)
#>         1         2         3         4         5         6 
#> 0.9004926 0.6447428 0.6861277 0.5879835 0.6954234 0.9432241 
colMeans(scores$curve)
#>      rnx5     rnx15     rnx40 
#> 0.6219815 0.7771177 0.9239052
